desc:
The digit sum of an integer is the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value, so the digit sum of -23 is 5 and that of 100 is 1.

Return nums sorted by digit sum in ascending order. Numbers with equal digit sums are ordered by value from largest to smallest.

Example: nums = [19, 100, 5, -23, 41] has digit sums 10, 1, 5, 5, 5. The number 100 comes first, then 41, 5, -23 (digit sum 5, larger first), and finally 19. The answer is [100, 41, 5, -23, 19].
hints: Define a function that turns a number into its digit sum, ignoring the sign.
The primary key is ascending, the tie-break is descending. A single sort key can mix both directions.
Use the key (digitSum(|x|), -x): negating the value turns the descending tie-break into an ascending one.
editorial: Compute the digit sum of |x| by repeatedly taking x % 10 and dividing by ten. The required order is: smaller digit sum first, and among equal digit sums the larger value first.
A key tuple (digitSum, -x) expresses both rules at once because negating the value reverses its direction. The sort costs O(n log n); computing the keys costs O(n) with at most ten digits per number.
